elements.element: Customer is not subject to any exclusivity or non-compete obligation.
elements.evidence: Ono remains prohibited from Commercializing or licensing defined Competing Products, although the new paragraph caps that restriction and adds a performance-based exit.

elements.element: Customer is not required to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 does not require Ono to purchase exclusively from Array or designate Array as its sole supplier.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies only to products falling within the expressly defined term “Competing Product,” comprising the specified active-ingredient categories and exclusions.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph states that Ono’s and its Affiliates’ obligations under Section 8.2 shall in no event continue beyond the twelve-month anniversary of the Effective Date.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly provides for automatic termination if Array fails to meet its Article 9 supply obligations, including any agreed or documented service levels.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly provides for automatic termination if Array fails to meet its Article 9 supply obligations, including any agreed or documented delivery dates.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Ono remains subject to a Competing Product non-compete. It fully achieves the fallback by limiting the restriction to the defined Competing Product category, imposing an absolute 12-month cap, and providing automatic termination for Array’s failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. Conforming Array’s termination right to apply only when Ono acts “in breach of this Section 8.2” is necessary to avoid a remedy after Ono’s obligations have expired, and no unrelated commercial terms are changed.
